claims.text: The as-deposited coating is a dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy coating.
The as-deposited coating has standard phase fractions and typical interphase-boundary characteristics.
Increasing FCC/BCC interphase-boundary coherence improves creep resistance.
Increasing dislocation pinning at FCC/BCC interphase boundaries improves creep resistance.
Improved boundary coherence and increased boundary dislocation density enhance the dislocation-pinning capacity of FCC/BCC interfaces.
Elevated temperature promotes creep deformation during sustained mechanical loading.
Enhanced FCC/BCC interphase-boundary properties provide stronger dislocation pinning.
Stronger interphase-boundary pinning restricts dislocation mobility during creep.
Restricted dislocation mobility reduces the rate of plastic deformation relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Coatings with improved interphase-boundary characteristics will exhibit a significantly lower creep rate than the as-deposited coating.
Coatings with improved interphase-boundary characteristics will accumulate less progressive plastic strain than the as-deposited coating.
The proposed interphase-boundary effect operates under sustained high stress and elevated temperature.
The proposed interphase-boundary effect may be diminished at low stress or room temperature.
The effectiveness of interface treatments may vary with subtle changes in alloy composition or processing conditions.
